development of thresholds. this seems to us a sensible approach. while developing the thresholds, we highlight. our understanding of this approach is that where there are significant uncertainties, comment_obs: thank you very much, mr. president, last week, on thursday, 20th of march of 2025 as you indicated, the council held an informal thematic discussion on the water cultural heritage, which interested members and observers of the authority. so during the discussion on 20th march, participants engaged on three questions. the first question asked whether the regulations should address under water cultural heritage, just in draft regulation 35 or 35 alt or take a broader approach to the issue. the participants who spoke on the question generally supported a broader approach to underwater cultural heritage, although a number of those participants focused their comments on thursday on draft regulation 35 and 35 alt the second question asked participants to indicate their preference for either draft regulation 35 alt or 35 as well as their comments for the text of vulnerable regulations. most participants who spoke generally prefer draft regulation 35 alt to 35 although there was mention of support for draft regulation 35 that's a reasonable compromise between the various interests at stake. participants also express views on whether the commission or the council should be tasked with various roles under draft regulation 35 or 35 alt whether to go with one or the other approaches to consultations in paragraph four or four alt and whether to compensate contractors who are impacted under the draft regulation, among other issues. the third question asked participants who support a broad approach to underwater cultural heritage to indicate what their views were on the purpose and substance of those other draft regulations, the participants who responded referred to on the water cultural heritage in, for example, environmental impact statements and the overall environmental impact process in emmp, in underwater cultural heritage management plans and baseline surveys of the seabed participants also highlighted the relevance of the 2001 2003 unesco conventions on underwater cultural heritage and intangible cultural heritage, respectively. although there was a comment that while the work done by unesco would be covered by unclos, in a sense, there is a question as to whether the authority as a specific entity is allowed under the convention to address on the water cultural heritage via the mining code. participants additionally discussed whether there should be a standalone committee on the water cultural heritage, those who spoke generally supported its creation, although i again stress that the discussion ran out of time before we could hear from all interested members of the authority on this and other issues. there were also issues or views expressed about the long standing cultural connections of various indigenous peoples and local communities to the ocean, including the deep sea and seabed. the point was made about the need for a reciprocal relationship between humankind and the deep sea seabed, as well as the notion of proper stewardship of the marine environment. a point was made about how pure, intangible, underwater cultural heritage, such as some of the examples expressed in the discussion, might not fit properly under the notion of underwater cultural heritage, but could be captured through other approaches, such as references to traditional knowledge, as well as the establishment of sites of particular cultural interest, there was also a bit of discussion on the issue of rights of indigenous peoples and of local communities, including their right to be consulted and involved in activities affecting them and their interests, with different and differing views expressed on the matter looking forward, my delegation believes that further work on underwater cultural heritage can and should be conducted by the council, including in an intersessional working group. there remain differences of views on how exactly to reflect this matter in the regulations, but there seems to be broad acceptance of the need to reflect these matters in some form and the regulations. there has also been genuine and respectful engagement on the matter for multiple corners for which i remain deeply grateful. i have also taken note of the proposed additional modality of work for the council going forward in the form of friends of the president, i recommend that this new modality, if implemented, should complement, rather than duplicate, the work of the underwater cultural heritage, intersession of working group and vice versa, assuming that the council agrees that the working group should continue its work, i stress that the working group has actually crafted and discussed possible textual proposals when on the water cultural heritage, rather than merely conducted high level thematic discussions. if the council now feels that the working group should stick to high level discussions and refrain from engaging on specific textual proposals in deference to the friends of the president, then it will be helpful to make this clear as soon as possible. similarly, if the council now wants to convert the working group into a friends of the president group to focus on just textual proposals, then it will also be helpful to make this clear as soon as possible. finally, in terms of the facilitation of the working group going forward, if it is to continue its work, i inform the council that after constructive discussions with the delegations of brazil and greece, i now wish to invite the delegations of brazil and greece to join my delegation in co facilitating the working group going forward, assuming again that the council wishes for the work to continue and for my delegation to continue, this will be in line with the practice already established with a number of other working groups, inter session, working groups of the council. thank you, mr. president.

day. dr nelson mandela was born on 18 july, 1918, in the village of invenso, of vessel in the eastern cape in south africa. and today would have been the 100 and seventh birthday celebration of a man justifiable economic and social development. mr. president, under the context of the exploration and potential exploitation of mineral resources found in the oceans, and taking into consideration a regulatory authority or enforceable law, alarming threats to the oceans face us because of such practices as the dumping of toxic waste over fishing or transnational crime like drug trafficking, the efforts to establish a workable legal order for the oceans must not fail, close quote, but significantly, nelson mandela continue to express that i quote. we do all know that there are no easy solution. we have to strike some difficult balances in the use of the oceans. close quote, mister president, these days an opportunity for the people to recognize their individual power to change the world for the better. and i hereby invite the international community present today, including the international organization, to also play an important part by raising awareness and expanding the reach of mandela's values, including the fight against injustice, helping people in need and advancing reconciliation.

observation: had 45 minutes speech prepared (joke), but wants to thank everyone and jamaica; french head of delegation's last meeting here, says goodbye
comment_obs: to the the i had prepared a 45 minute presentation, which i don't think i'll have the time to read. so i'll improvise, as i usually do, and say mostly just whatever i would like to speak for 45 minutes, just to say bye, bye, or tsai tian, or see you soon. and this is, these are my last minutes at the seabed authority. i worked here between 2012 and 2016 and when i asked to be the ambassador in jamaica, i had asked for jamaica because i had fallen in love with jamaica, and i also returned to jamaica because i wanted to come back to my family here at the isa, and i found old friends like pedro olav, and i apologize to all of the others who i haven't mentioned, and i am leaving with a great deal of sadness for all of the wonderful moments we've spent together. and what we do here is historic, because we work to regulate an activity that hasn't begun yet. this is the first time in history that we are beginning to regulate, or that we are attempting to regulate, an activity which has not yet commenced, and that's why it takes time for us to understand exactly what the conditions are going to be, what the consequences are going to be. we have to understand what the effects of this activity on the environment are going to be, to understand what the economic benefits are going to be as well, and how we should make sure that it is all of humanity that benefits from this. i also want to take this opportunity to remember the dear friends. these are not friends that are no longer here. they're still alive. but i remember jean pierre le vi and eli jamas who, in terms of the work of the authority, absolutely taught me so many, many things, and it's a wonderful world that we are find ourselves in today, with this new secretary general, which we have full trust and confidence in, with a new vision as well about the work that can be done on future regulations, i leave jamaica, i leave the authority, but the authority in jamaica will be forever in my heart.

- Example key words: research, science, knowledge, scientific

- Example key words: environment, precautionary, protect, preserve, moratorium

- For each vision, provide:
  1. A probability between 0 and 1 (up to 2 decimal places) indicating how strongly the statement reflects the vision.

actor: international tribunal for the law of the sea
observation: speech
comment_obs: your excellencies, distinguished delegates, ladies and gentlemen, it is a great honor for me to address you today, on the occasion of the 30th anniversary of the international seabed authority, this is a milestone, not only for the authority, but for the international community as a whole. it marks three decades of commitment to the effective multilateral governance of the area and its resources, which form the common heritage of humankind. the establishment of the authority was a bold and missionary step in the development of international law, an embodiment of the spirit of cooperation, enshrined in the united nations convention on the law of the sea, it created, for the first time, a robust institutional framework for the management of mineral resources beyond national jurisdiction, ensuring that their exploration and exploitation would be carried out for the benefit of all. as we reflect on this legacy, i would like to highlight the important role of the seabed disputes chamber, which acts as a specialized judicial body within the international tribunal for the law of the sea. its role is twofold to settle disputes concerning activities in the area and to give advisory opinions at the request of the assembly or the council of the authority legal questions arising within the scope of their activities, dispute chamber has already demonstrated its utility in this regard. in 2011 at the request of the council, the chamber issued an advisory opinion. it's clarified in considerable detail the responsibilities and obligations of states sponsoring comment_obs: mr. president, madam secretary-general, excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, i am honored to deliver this statement on behalf of fiji, jamaica, singapore and my country, malta. it is a privilege to participate in this milestone celebration of the 30th anniversary of the international seabed authority. as part of this commemorative this commemoration, we present you a draft decision for adoption by the assembly declaring first november as international day of the deep seabed. this draft decision embraces a strong multilateral spirit that brings us together this assembly and communicates a positive message to the world. the draft decision is not intended to be overly prescriptive or technical, but rather provides a space for isa members and the international community to reflect. in this reflection, i pay tribute to some of the key figures who were instrumental in the creation and evolution of the united nations convention on the law of the sea and the international seabed authority, malta's own arvid pardo, who, on first november 1967 envisioned and introduced the powerful and enduring principle of the common heritage of mankind, now enshrined in unclos, and which ultimately led to the establishment of the isa fiji's late ambassador, satya nandans enduring legacy on the genesis of unclos and the establishment of the isa, serving as his inaugural inaugural secretary general, jamaica as host country of the isa, as well as the outstanding contribution of the late doctor, the honorable kenneth rattery to the law of the sea unclos and isa, the plenary conference room in which we are meeting, was renamed in his honor in 2007 singapore's own ambassador tomicor, who was instrumental in shaping unclos and driving the negotiations on unclos to their successful conclusion, fiji, jamaica, malta and singapore carry this torch forward, along with every isa member state. here in the room today, we all play a crucial role as joint custodians of the deep seabed. and 30 years from on, from the establishment of the isa, the momentum has grown, and together, we cooperate in trust towards the conservation and sustainable use of the ocean in accordance with unclos, the legal framework from which all activities in the oceans and sea must be carried forward this international day of the deep seabed can promote global awareness of the importance of the deep seabed as the area beyond national jurisdiction, the area covering around half of the total area of the world's oceans. indeed, this day provides a space for the isa and its member states to consider and discuss various positive elements, the principle of the common heritage of mankind, the role of the legal regime for the area, as set out in unclos and the 1994 agreement on the implementation of part 11 of unclos, which has established the rule of law in the area, including with respect to the conservation and sustainable use and prevented the unbridled exploitation of its mineral resources. the importance of the iss mandate to elaborate and conglo conclude rules, regulations and procedures relating to the exploitation of the mineral resources of the area, which will provide the regulatory framework to ensure the orderly conducts of mineral resource related activities and the effective protection of the marine environment. the role of the isa in advancing deep-sea research, harnessing science and technology and building the capacity of developing countries towards advancing global knowledge and understanding of the area for informed decision making, the work of the isa in support of the achievement of the sustainable development goals. after consultation with isa member states, we are delighted that this drove decision can now be adopted by consensus as a signal to the global community that the resolve to conserve and sustainably use the deep seabed is as strong as ever. thank you. thank you.

eventually adopt rules, regulations and procedures relating to exploitation of mineral resources in the area. we recognize that the council has been taking some time to elaborate the exploitation regulations, given their complexity and importance. singapore has been actively participating in this process in good faith to ensure that the exploitation regulations are sufficiently robust as befits regulating activities that concern the common heritage of mankind. we welcome the good progress made during the 30th council meetings, in particular the completion of the second reading of the consolidated text and dynamic and productive thematic discussions, including via defense of the president initiative. we further note that a subsidiary of the metals company applied for permits under isa. we also wish to reiterate that the convention and the 1994 agreement affirm that the area and its resources are the common heritage of humankind, a concept so fundamental that it is commonly considered customary international law. no state may claim appropriate nor exercise sovereignty or sovereign rights over any part of the area or its resources. at the same time, states parties should not be undermining the work of the authority, which has been carried out in accordance with the convention and the 1994 agreement. we heard in a statement made earlier yesterday, a reference to gambling to fail to fulfill our obligations under the convention to develop and adopt robust exploitation regulations will be to leave the door open for unregulated exploitation of the mineral resources of the area which the convention and the 1994 agreement sought to prevent, mr. president, this to us would be considered gambling with the common heritage of humankind that there will be no unregulated exploitation in the absence of exploitation regulations, the convention and the 1994 agreement are one package any selectivity in their implementation and any violation of the common heritage principle would risk under mining the integrity of the legal framework for the ocean that is founded upon these treaties, the authority and the rules based multilateral system, this will not be in the interest of any country. singapore reaffirms our position that deep seabed mining should not commence before robust regulations are adopted, in particular, those intended to ensure effective protection of the marine environment, along with our fellow members of the authority singapore, will continue to work on elaborating the exploitation regulations in good faith. these recent developments are a timely reminder for members to continue to work together to expedite the conclusion of the elaboration of the exploitation regulations, and to ensure that the regulator of the seabed has regulations to fulfill its purpose, this is not only our obligation, but the most effective safeguard for the marine environment and the clearest demonstration of our commitment to the principles of the convention.

information system or bis. the report notes that the deep data repository follows fair principles, findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable. however, the repository could be further improved in relation to findability and usability of environmental data and information. we are heartened to see the secretary's collaboration and cooperation with international scientific and technical bodies policy makers. likewise, dosi appreciates the deep-sea biobank initiative, creating a repository of biological samples from the area, and we look forward to learning more. we hope that it facilitates access to samples and data sharing and creates further collaboration opportunities with the bbnj agreement, we appreciate the secretariat's fact check documents that attempt to synergize key topics related to the marine environment, but we know that at least some of these documents contain inaccuracies we want to highlight and command the first steps taken by the secretariat towards a collaborative review and correction of these documents with appropriate expertise to which dosi has been invited to collaborate. we look forward to seeing the final product and to further collaborative efforts in the same direction, we acknowledge and commend the progress made in the understanding of the impacts of nodule collectors, as highlighted in paragraph 24 but wish to highlight that the results of single, small scale experiments do not provide an accurate understanding of the effects of commercial mining on the marine environment. furthermore, we would like to stress that there is not a single study that validates the discharge of plume models or deals with their effects in the pelagic environment. this is one example of the many knowledge gaps that still remain in the assessment of impacts of deep-sea mining, as we have done before, dosi emphasizes that, based on our current scientific understanding of the ocean, deep seabed mining will result in biodiversity loss and irreversible harm to deep-sea ecosystems, including changes to the functions and services they provide, scientists have just begun to understand biodiversity, ecosystem functions, oceanography, processes and resilience in the areas targeted for mining, with many gaps remaining. thus, the international community is currently not yet in a position to reliably predict the extent and severity of ecosystem services such as genetic resources, climate regulation or commercially important fisheries, available tools such as scientific models that can help to predict impact require robust, robust baseline data, they're not yet available, and small scale in situ tests to verify these models only go so far. deep-sea scientific research is majorly unexplored areas, and the incorporation of this take the best collaborative efforts to promote strengthen and conduct ocean science.

observation: 45 days notice + 8 weeks of un translation is the reason for the current dates; ...

comment_obs: thank you very much. mr. president excellencies, distinguished delegates, i have the honor to deliver this statement on behalf of the african group. at the outset, we express our sincere appreciation to the interim director general of the enterprise, ambassador eden charles for his detailed report of the activities undertaken and progress made during the period of july 2024, to may 2025, in particular, the african group wishes to commend the interim dg for his active participation during the negotiations of the draft regulations, and we are confident of his leadership and ability to oversee the performance of the functions of the enterprise until it begins to operate independently. we take note in paragraph 6c of the report, the interim dg has mandate to support development of projects in cooperation with developing states for improving scientific understanding of the area. in furtherance of this, perhaps during the coming year, the enterprise could provide some forward thinking insights on opportunities relating to marine scientific research project development and plans for consideration. mr. president, with reference to paragraph 15 and 16 regarding monitoring and review of trends in the mining activity mining industry, we wonder if any reports from the meeting of the international nickel study group, the international copper study group and the international lead and zinc study group, which the interim dg attended in order to obtain accurate and timely information on capacities, production, usage, trade, stocks, prices, technologies, research and development and other factors that may influence the supply and demands of metals could be reported back to the cancer. this might be especially useful for the work of the soon to be established economic and planning commission. the african group continues to emphasize the need to further operationalize the enterprise in the step wise approach, as it remains, the principal vehicle for the effective participation of developing states in activities in the area. the african group has taken note of the interim dg update on the preliminary work undertaken since july 2024 to conceptualize a structured and policy driven organizational model for the enterprise we wish, the african group wishes to underscore that as we approach the finalization of the exploitation regulation, the operationalization of the enterprise must move beyond conceptual planning and into tangible, time bound implementation. the enterprise is a critical pillar in ensuring the realization of the common heritage of humankind and its effective establishment. it's central to upholding equity and the interest of developing states under part 11 of the convention. accordingly, we urge that the next phase of work focus on delivering concrete outcomes that demonstrate measurable progress towards full operational capability. this includes, but it's not limited, to the recruitment of dedicate, dedicated technical and legal personnel, the formal establishment of of its internal governance and financial management systems, the development of a strategy for participating, for participation in joint ventures, and the commencement of preparatory work for potential exploration and exploitation activities, the full and timely establishment of the enterprise is essential to ensure equity capacity building and technology transfer as critical elements of the exploitation regime envisioned by unclos. this strategy, this strategic priority, reflects our firm commitment to upholding the principle of the common heritage of humankind in the governance and exploitation of the deep-sea mineral resources. in this regard, the african group supports the full operationalisation of the enterprise as a commercially oriented entity functioning with a degree of autonomy under the general policies of the assembly and the directives of the council of the international seabed authority, the african group remains committed to supporting this process and calls for a clear and measurable road map to ensure enterprise is positioned to discharge its mandate in accordance with comment_obs: first of all, we'd like to thank chile for including this item to the agenda, which is un finished business from the 29th session of the assembly and deserves further consideration. in our view, it is entirely appropriate for the assembly to establish a general policy on the protection and preservation of the marine environment. the assembly is the supreme organ of the authority, and has the power to establish general policies on any question or matter within the competence of the authority, in collaboration with the council, article 145 provides an undisputable legal basis for the elaboration of a general policy on the protection and preservation of the marine environment. there will be no overlap between the general policy and the regulations. such a policy will establish the overall plan and the general environmental goals in the area, setting priorities and providing guidance in light of new circumstances and challenges in accordance with the precautionary principle. it will also ensure consistency between the different organs of the authority on environmental issues, and will provide the framework within which all relevant issues will be discussed, including the widespread concerns about environmental impacts of deep-sea mining or moving to exploitation before sufficient scientific evidence is available to clearly demonstrate that such operations will not result in adverse impact to the marine environment. we agree with brazil that the general policy will also align the efforts of the authority with other international instruments and fora, in particular, with the bbnj agreement, which will also be applicable to the area once it enters into force. we are aware that there are different views between the delegations, both on the need and the scope and parameters of a general policy. however, at this stage, we are not considering the adoption of a general policy, but the establishment of an informal intersessional dialog to discuss these issues, including procedural issues. it would be regrettable it would not be possible to agree even on such an initial step. turning now to the revised draft proposal. we are not in favor of the proposed amendments in sub paragraphs a and b of paragraph four of the draft decision, and more specifically, with a reference to paragraph four section three of the annex to the agreement. in our view, the reference in paragraph one section three of the annex in collaboration with the council, does not imply that the process for the liberation of a general policy should be initiated through a recommendation of the council. however, since there is a divergence of views on the interpretation of these provisions at this stage, we would prefer to leave this issue open and do not make any reference to any particular provision in paragraph four subparagraphs a and b of the draft decision, the procedure for the establishment of a general policy will be one of the main issues to be discussed during the intersessional dialog.

observation: very grateful to chile; assembly is supreme organ with power to establish gps; it should not be controversial for assembly to informally discuss; does not accept any counterarguments given; either way, this can be discussed in intersessional dialogue; not even considering a gp is a bad look
comment_obs: ireland is very grateful to chile for its proposal for the assembly to establish an informal intersessional dialog to facilitate further discussion and general policy for the protection and preservation of the marine environment. ireland strongly supports this proposal. the assembly is the supreme organ of the authority, and it has the power to establish general policies on any question or matter within the competence of the authority, as long as those policies are in conformity with unclos, considering that one of the main objectives of the convention is the protection and preservation of the marine environment to which part 12 is dedicated, it should not be controversial for the assembly to informally discuss a general policy to give effect to this obligation. in ireland's view, a general policy for the protection and preservation of the marine environment would give effect to the provisions of article 145 of the convention, and would facilitate coordination and harmonization between the provisions of the convention and the activities of the authority. a general policy would also enable consistency and mutual supportiveness between the organs of the authority, while ireland acknowledges that any decision of the assembly to establish a general policy shall be in collaboration with the council. ireland is of the view that the adoption of the draft decision would be consistent with the distribution of powers and functions among the organs of the authority. this decision, rather than establishing a general policy, simply provides time and space for member states to exchange views on the necessity and content of a potential general policy. moreover, the draft decision specifically provides for engagement with the council, consistent with the 94 agreement. various arguments have been put forward by some space states in opposition to this proposal. they suggest that the trespasses into the matters that are the responsibility of the ltc and the council, that it risks distracting from the mining code, that it will prejudice the mining code, and that the exploitation regulations are sufficient to address environmental concerns. ireland does not accept any of these arguments. in any event, these are all issues that can be further discussed within the intersessional dialog, which, i reiterate, does not provide for the adoption of a general policy, merely a process to consider one at a time when the authority is under considerable international scrutiny, when we are moving towards a potential exploitation phase, and when widespread concerns persist about the environmental impacts of deep-sea mining. it would be highly regrettable if this modest proposal were to be blocked once again by some states, such an outcome would call into question the credibility of the authority as a regulator committed to the protection of the marine environment. it would send a lamentable signal to the outside world. not only will the authority not adopt a general environmental policy, it will not even consider it. this is not a good look. ireland urges the members of the assembly to support the draft decision.

An **institutional vision** is a conception of the ISA’s future purpose, authority, legitimacy, or role within global ocean governance.
You will read a single negotiation statement and evaluate how strongly it reflects each of three institutional visions of the ISA:

- Example key words: mineral resources, mining, exploitation, mining code, extraction
2. **Marine scientific research institution** — ISA as a multilateral scientific institution coordinating deep-sea research.
- Example key words: research, science, knowledge, scientific

- Example key words: environment, precautionary, protect, preserve, moratorium

### Instructions

- For each vision, provide:
  1. A probability between 0 and 1 (up to 2 decimal places) indicating how strongly the statement reflects the vision.

- Focus on how the statement positions the ISA, not merely on topical keywords.  
- Include imaginaries that are explicit or implicit, including affirmations of current role.
